claim_findings.basis_reference: Reduced-fraction representation theorem: every rational number r can be written r=a/b for integers a,b with b ≠ 0 and gcd(a,b)=1. Its hypothesis is claim-rational-assumption, and it is applied in step-lowest-terms.
Derived by the arithmetic and parity arguments in step-a-even and step-b-even.
The contradiction in step-contradiction discharges the local rationality assumption.

objection_history.attack: Check whether the rationality assumption is confined to a reductio subproof and actually discharged.
Check that the named lowest-terms representation theorem applies to the assumed rational number and supplies all required conditions.
Check the parity inference and the division implicit in deriving b²=2m².
Check whether the contradiction genuinely negates rationality rather than merely contradicting an arbitrary choice of a and b.
Check whether the temporary rationality assumption is used outside its reductio scope or left undis­charged.
Check the reduced-fraction theorem's hypothesis and whether it supplies all stated properties.
Check the parity inference, including the division used to obtain b²=2m².
Check that the contradiction actually refutes rationality rather than merely the selected representation.
